stem: A nurse on a hospital stroke quality-improvement team notes that performance on STK-2, Discharged on Antithrombotic Therapy, has declined. Which action best uses this quality-measure information?

options.A: Review eligible ischemic-stroke cases against the STK-2 discharge-prescribing criteria and documented exclusions to identify process gaps for improvement.
options.B: Assume every ischemic-stroke discharge without an antithrombotic prescription represents an error, regardless of documented reasons for nonprescribing.
options.C: Use the aggregate STK-2 rate to determine which individual bedside nurse caused each missed prescription without reviewing the records.
options.D: Replace individualized discharge decisions with the measure numerator so that all stroke clients receive the same medication plan.

rationale: The Joint Commission's current STK-2 measure evaluates ischemic-stroke patients prescribed antithrombotic therapy at discharge and includes a pathway for documented reasons for not prescribing therapy. A quality-improvement review should therefore examine eligible cases against the defined measure criteria and exclusions to identify process gaps. B ignores valid documented exclusions, C attributes causation from an aggregate measure without case review, and D misuses a performance measure as a substitute for individualized clinical decision-making.
educational_objective: Use stroke performance-measure data for structured quality improvement by reviewing eligible cases against the measure's defined criteria and exclusions rather than treating the metric as a substitute for individualized care or as proof of individual fault.
source_document_title: Specifications Manual for Joint Commission National Quality Measures (v2026B) — STK-2: Discharged on Antithrombotic Therapy
source_locator: Stroke (STK) Measure Information Form, STK-2, version 2026B: Performance Measure Name/Description; numerator and denominator logic; algorithm step 'Reason for Not Prescribing Antithrombotic Therapy at Discharge.' Applies to discharges 07-01-2026 through 12-31-2026.
source_claim_supported: Directly defines STK-2 as a stroke process-performance measure based on antithrombotic prescribing at discharge and explicitly accounts for documented reasons for nonprescribing, supporting case review against measure criteria rather than automatic classification of every nonprescription as an error.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Appendix A → Safe and Effective Care Environment → Management of Care → Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement), printed PDF page 22/file page 25: define performance-improvement/quality-assurance activities; participate in performance-improvement projects and quality-improvement processes; utilize research/references for performance-improvement actions; evaluate the impact of performance-improvement measures on client care and resource use.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement) using stroke process-measure data
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item around the current Joint Commission 2026B STK-2 specification instead of the generic CMS/AHA homepage. Removed the vague claim that all listed measures are simply 'shown to improve outcomes' and replaced it with a directly testable nursing quality-improvement action using the measure's actual eligibility and exclusion logic.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Stroke quality measurement and nursing performance improvement
audit_findings.source_authority: Current Joint Commission national quality-measure specification for STK-2; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan for the nursing quality-improvement construct.
audit_findings.currentness: Joint Commission v2026B was posted February 6, 2026 and applies to July 1 through December 31, 2026 discharges, matching the current audit period.

claim_by_claim.stem: STK-2 is a current Joint Commission Stroke measure titled 'Discharged on Antithrombotic Therapy.'
claim_by_claim.A: Correct because the measure specification defines eligible ischemic-stroke cases, the discharge-prescribing numerator, and documented reasons for nonprescribing; reviewing these criteria is a valid QI use of the measure.
claim_by_claim.B: Incorrect because STK-2 explicitly accounts for a documented reason for not prescribing antithrombotic therapy at discharge.
claim_by_claim.C: Incorrect because aggregate measure performance does not by itself establish individual causation; the NCSBN QI construct supports systematic review and improvement rather than unsupported attribution.
claim_by_claim.D: Incorrect because a performance measure evaluates a defined process and does not replace individualized clinical decision-making or contraindication/exclusion assessment.
claim_by_claim.rationale: Uses only the current STK-2 measure logic and NCSBN quality-improvement role; no unsupported outcome magnitude, medication dose, or universal treatment claim is introduced.
claim_by_claim.educational_objective: Specific to interpreting and acting on a current stroke process measure in a nursing quality-improvement context.

audit_findings.distractor_audit: B, C, and D are plausible misuse patterns for quality metrics—ignoring exclusions, attributing causation without review, and replacing clinical judgment with a metric. Each is distinct and clearly inferior to A.
audit_findings.ambiguity_and_second_answer: Only A follows both the current STK-2 specification and the NCSBN performance-improvement activity statements. No second option remains defensible as the best action.
audit_findings.cueing: Options are comparable in specificity and all describe an action; the keyed option is not identified by grammar, length alone, or unique technical jargon.
audit_findings.blueprint: Directly maps to 2026 NCSBN Management of Care → Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement).
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Re-read the source specification and item without relying on the original key; challenged whether B could be defended by a simple numerator interpretation and whether D represented protocolized care. The explicit STK-2 nonprescribing-reason logic and NCSBN QI construct make A uniquely best, with no unresolved conflict.
